I'd love to hear if there are other suggestions out there as well.

Best,
Alison

messages.author: 91fcdff1323a6831
messages.subject: Re: 3d plots (of streamflow data)
parts:
Hi Meghan,

Is there a particular reason to use the 3d view? You could easily use facets in ggplot to plot the same data and it may be easier to interpret because there wouldn't be data potentially obstructed by layers in front. You would certainly have many more options if you considered dropping the 3D requirement, and it might be easier to interpret for the reader. However, if you are keen to visualize in 3d, I've used persp a bit as well, but for xyz surface plots of topography. One new package which is really fun to use, though more for exploratory purposes is "plot_ly".  

As an example here's some code you could try using your data. You can export as PNG from the plot itself (if you click small button and open in a browser it will be easier to do than in RStudio).  The included snapshot is from a bigger dataset I used of some 3d bar topography data, but grouped by the scan location.

## Create data (this is just pasted from a random flow/temp dataset)
x <- seq(1,25,1)
y <- c(8.036730769, 7.829166667, 8.482916667, 9.4690625, 10.5978125, 11.4896875, 11.86989583, 
       11.70260417, 11.37947917, 10.479375, 9.987395833, 10.0953125, 9.593333333, 9.5659375, 10.02875, 
       10.3746875, 10.12479167, 9.889791667, 9.491458333, 9.259583333, 9.956041667, 10.16895833, 10.3225, 
       11.8078125, 12.21947917)
z <- c(2.443436087, 4.369033438, 6.766952479, 4.176211145, 2.539315738, 4.554630615, 3.852905435, 4.27978627, 
       2.293411763, 4.339267628, 4.245072739, 3.644484732, 5.866500184, 5.475036304, 5.029551926, 2.199508359, 
       4.404874198, 4.991906775, 2.162372383, 2.901433674, 2.363337489, 9.884017923, 5.277798281, 3.074637322,13.5933143)

site<-c(rep("NFA",5), rep("MFA",5), rep("SFA",5), rep("NFY",5),rep("MFY",5)) # make site names, this could be year
df<-data.frame(x, y, z, site)

library(plotly)
with(df, plot_ly(x=x,y=y,z=z, group=site, type="scatter3d"))


Hope this helps,
Adios,
Ryan

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: 3d plots (of streamflow data)
parts:
Hi Meghan,

I would second Ryan and suggest you consider not using a 3D plot. 

Personally, I find the second graph in "example.png" to be a bit of a nightmare to read - it is difficult to compare years because the 3D perspective messes with the relative heights of the peaks, features are obscured in cases where a large peak is in front of a smaller valley, etc. It might not be so bad with only 4 years of data, but even then I am not sure what you would gain over a simpler graph style (in terms of ease of reading). 

Matt

I will look into persp and image2D, but I will also try to multi-panel approach.  

Meghan
